newsitem.title: USA: Olin sees $150 million from divestitures.
newsitem.headline: Olin sees $150 million from divestitures.

text.p: Olin Corp said Thursday it expected to receive about $150 million in after-tax net cash from the sale of two of its companies in a sweeping restructuring of the company.
The sale of its isocyanates and polyol, glycol and surfactants businesses is one of a series of what the company has described as "strategic initiatives" to concentrate its operations.
"We will be more tightly focused," it said. "We will be ... better positioned to achieve our goals of increasing shareholder value while doubling our 1995 earnings per share by the year 2000."
Some of the other initiatives include spinning off its Ordnance and Aerospace divisions and a two-for-one stock split.

Olin said it will sell its isocyanates businesses in Lake Charles, La to ARCO Chemical Co for $565 million in cash and start looking for a buyer for the other businesses at its Doe Run facility in Brandenburg, Ky.
"We expect that these divestitures, Lake Charles and Doe Run together, will generate net cash proceeds in the $400 million range and an after tax gain approximating $150 million," it said.
Headquartered in Norwalk, Conn, Olin is one of the world's leading producers of chemicals, metals, microelectronic materials, sporting and military ammunition, and aerospace products.
It employs about 13,000 people and has 1995 sales of $3.2 billion.
